exposure: Birth weight difference of more than 1000g between first and second delivery
cohort: Women who had their first and second live fetus singleton delivery at a single large academic center between 2005 and 2019. Women who had cesarean delivery at first delivery were excluded.
finding: Birth weight interval ≥1000 g between the first and second delivery is associated with higher rates of cesarean deliveries, as well as an increase in maternal and neonatal adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was more prevalent among the study group (7.9% vs 3.2%, aOR 3.31 [1.78-6.17], p < .001), including in-labor cesarean delivery (3.2% vs 1.5%, aOR 2.97 [1.46-6.06], p = .01)
birth_weight: Neonates with inter-delivery birth weight interval ≥1000 g from their first delivery
